The City provides a grant for one time capital project funding through the Cultural Grant Capital Reserve. This grant program was developed in 2013 and provides funding for up to 50% of the total capital project cost. This grant is available to organizations who are currently in the Cultural Grant Program. The grants are awarded based on recommendations made by the education

committee in accordance with the policy. The education committee met in November of 2024 and recommended that a total of 100,000 in funding be awarded to three organizations on board staging. Good morning. My name is Shannon Jostell and I'm the Executive Director of the Saskatchewan Jazz Festival.
I'm here to speak to the committee about the 2025 Cultural Grant Capital Reserve Awards and the recommended award for our organizations rebrand project.
The Saskatchewan Jazz Festival was started in 1987 by an enthusiastic group of volunteer jazz fans from the Saskatoon Jazz Society.
Today it has become the second largest festival of its kind in western Canada. And since 2009 has been named Best Festival in Planet S Magazine's Best of Saskatoon Reader School.
In 2023 we were named venue or festival of the year of the Saskatchewan Music Awards and were nominated for the 2024 Canadian Live Music Industry Awards in the major festival of the year category.
Since 2023 the festival has also been named Best Place to Volunteer by Planet S Magazine's Best of Saskatoon Reader School.
We employ a permanent staff of three, two year round contractors, four seasonal employees, and recruit upwards of four amazing volunteers annually.

We are proud to be a major contributor to the cultural economy through our substantial employment of local artists, technicians and suppliers, and both an annual economic impact of approximately $8 million.
We are a registered charity with a mission to foster, promote, and present jazz and related contemporary genres to the people of Saskatchewan.

These include initiatives like our Jazz Intensive Summer Camp presented in partnership with the University of Saskatchewan and our Care Home Outreach Program presented in partnership with a spirit retirement living.
We also present 75% of all programming free of charge to the public as part of our commitment to community and artistic accessibility.
The past five years have brought some of the most substantial challenges and changes in our organization's 38-year history.
The effects of the COVID-19 pandemic and the resulting shutdowns have had a well-documented impact on the cultural and live events sector, and we were certainly not immune.

After finally being able to return to full-scale operations in 2022 we were presented with a new rental agreement from our longtime venue that was financially unsustainable and necessitated our move to our current home in Victoria Park.
We have been fortunate to find a great deal of success and positive reception in our new home and are excited by the opportunities for growth we see on the horizon.
However, as we moved into our 2024 season we were presented with one more substantial change.
After nearly three decades as title sponsor, Sask tell notified us that they would not renew their title sponsorship agreement for 2026.
To be clear, Sask tell remains a valued partner and major sponsor of the festival.
We are immensely grateful for their decades of support and look forward to more years of partnership with them.
But with the title sponsorship position vacant, our organization now requires a substantial rebranding effort.
This includes everything from our logo, graphics and website to larger festival infrastructure, including our main stage,
stream and page entry, festival banners and even directional signage.
In addition, a substantial amount of research and community consultation will be included in the project or a reflection of our commitment to the people and community we serve.

As a flagship cultural grant recipient, the Saskatchewan Jazz Festival is grateful for the continued support of the City of Saskatoon and especially for the recommended award from the Cultural Grant Capital Reserve that is up for approval this morning.
This award covers 42% of the total rebranding costs which allows us to undertake this essential project without affecting programming capacity or delivery.
We are also pleased to share that all of the consultants and suppliers employed by this project are local to Saskatoon keeping the awarded funds here in the community.
In closing, I would like to sincerely thank the committee for their attention to these awards and the immense difference they make for us and our colleagues in the Cultural Grant Program.

I would also like to extend our appreciation to the City of Saskatoon for their continued support of our organization and recognition of the essential rule arts and cultural organizations play in our daily lives community and economy.
